verdict.headline: US strikes near Strait of Hormuz send oil surging ahead of jobs week
verdict.label: HOLD — 0 of 2 regime triggers active: 30Y 5.17% (5.30% gate clear); BTC $77,481 (above $62K floor). No US equity session Sunday; US military action near Hormuz adds oil-inflation overhang into Monday's open.
verdict.rationale_short: No US equity session Sunday. BTC has drifted lower to $77,481 at 8pm ET (Crypto.com live; 24h range $76,988–$79,409), down from Saturday's $78,153 — the five-attempt $80K resistance conversion remains unmet and the risk-off tone from the Iran strike is a modest additional headwind. The dominant Sunday night story: US forces hit Iranian rocket launchers at Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, ending roughly a month of relative quiet in the ongoing 2026 Hormuz campaign. Brent crude surged above $90/barrel and WTI hit ~$86 (+2% at open); S&P 500 futures slipped 0.1% Sunday night. The geopolitical escalation opens an oil-CPI channel at the worst possible moment — Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech already has September hike odds at 59–68%, and a sustained oil-driven inflation impulse is the mechanism that would push the 30Y the 13bps remaining to the 5.30% regime trigger. Friday's equity snapshot (S&P –0.25%, Nasdaq –0.52%) is unchanged. Wall Street is on pace for a positive August (Dow +2.1% for the month entering Monday), but that month-end tailwind competes directly with the geopolitical risk premium and the jobs-week calendar: August BLS (Sept 4, 8:30am ET) is the rate-path binary — above 200K payrolls with AHE above 0.3% plus oil-driven CPI risk assembles a full hawkish tableau and likely cements the September hike.

trade_setups.asset: Energy / Oil — Brent above $90 on Hormuz escalation
trade_setups.thesis: US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers at Larak Island ended ~1 month of Hormuz calm and sent Brent above $90 (+2% at Sunday open). The 2026 Hormuz campaign has disrupted shipping since late February; each military re-escalation has added 2–4% to crude in the first 48 hours before partially fading. If Brent sustains above $90, the CPI read-through is meaningful for Fed rate expectations and tightens the September hike calculus. Long energy into Monday's open is the tactical play; the invalidation is a swift diplomatic de-escalation announcement that reverses the premium.
trade_setups.entry: Brent ~$90, WTI ~$86 Sunday night. Hold above $90 Monday close sustains the risk premium.
trade_setups.invalidation: Diplomatic ceasefire or Hormuz re-opening announcement; Brent back below $87.

trade_setups.asset: 2Y-30Y Treasury spread — oil adds upward pressure on the 30Y trigger
trade_setups.thesis: Spread entered the week at ~85bps (30Y 5.17% minus 2Y 4.32%). The Iran-driven oil surge adds an inflationary channel that could push the 30Y toward the 5.30% regime trigger. If Brent holds above $90 into the August jobs report (Sept 4) and payrolls come in above 200K with AHE above 0.3%, the combined oil-CPI + hot-payrolls input likely cements September hike and tests 5.30% on the 30Y. The two-indicator framework (30Y gate + BTC floor) currently reads 0-of-2 triggered; a hot jobs print plus sustained oil could change that.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y at ~5.17% Friday close. Watch 5.25% as the early warning level; 5.30% is the hard regime gate.
trade_setups.invalidation: August payrolls below 150K with AHE below 0.2%; Brent fades below $87. Both together reverse hike odds and take 30Y durably below 5.00%.
trade_setups.horizon: Monday August 31 through September 4 (jobs report), September 16 (FOMC)

bear_case: The Hormuz escalation assembles the most complete bear scenario in the 2026 framework: (1) Oil above $90 adds a real CPI impulse on top of already-elevated services inflation; (2) Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech has September hike odds at 59–68%, and oil-driven CPI makes any near-term pivot language impossible; (3) The 30Y sits just 13bps from the 5.30% regime trigger — a sustained inflationary oil shock is the mechanism that closes that gap; (4) BTC has failed five consecutive $80K conversion attempts and trades at $77,481, removing the crypto momentum narrative; (5) The August jobs report (Sept 4) compares against July's –23K miss, meaning even a modest rebound above 150K with solid AHE reads as 'strong' and cements the September hike. If payrolls rebound above 200K, AHE above 0.3%, and Brent holds above $90 — the first simultaneous stagflation reading (cost-push inflation + tightening labor = hot CPI + negative real growth signal) assembles in real time. The 30Y tests 5.30%, the 2Y-30Y spread compresses below 75bps, equities price the hike, and BTC retraces toward $74K. The level that flips this read: a Hormuz de-escalation that takes Brent back below $85, combined with a soft jobs print (below 100K, AHE flat) — that binary would push September hike odds below 30% and open a rate-compression rally.
